Classify domestic animals into ruminants, monogastrics and poultry
Give examples of animals classified as ruminants, monogastrics, and poultry
Discuss and write the differences among ruminants, monogastrics and poultry
Write similarities in the nature and characteristics of ruminants, monogastrics and poultry in Ghana and other countries

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.2.4.2: Show an understanding of the usefulness of the different types of animals for domestic and commercial purposes
Indicator: Discuss and write the domestic and commercial uses of different types of animals
Exemplars:
Explain the concepts of domestic use and commercial use of animals
Make a poster of any two domestic animals that are useful and describe a narrative or extended answer while speaking the domestic uses of ruminants, monogastrics and poultry

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.2.4.2: Show an understanding of the usefulness of the different types of animals for domestic and commercial purposes
Indicator: Observe and compare the uses of the different types of animals
Exemplars:
Make a research on animals in your communities by observing them and discuss their different uses
List and match the different domestic animals to their commercial uses including their by-products (such as animal waste)

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.1.1: Show an understanding of the concept of food, and the process of digestion and appreciate its importance in humans
Indicator: Explain the concept of food and the need for humans to eat
Exemplars:
Explain what food is, the nutrients found in them and deduce its definition
Compare and contrast the appearance of people who have been starved for some period of time with those who have been eating and look healthy and strong. 3. Deduce from the comparison in 2 the importance of feeding in humans

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.1.1: Show an understanding of the concept of food, and the process of digestion and appreciate its importance in humans
Indicator: Examine what happens to food at the stages of digestion in humans
Exemplars:
Identify the parts of the alimentary canal in a drawing of the digestive system
Research and describe what happens to food e.g. a piece of boiled yam / cassava / plantain / cocoyam / bread, egg, meat, orange, palm oil andmany others when it gets into the mouth, stomach, large and small intestines
Draw and label the digestive system of humans

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.1.1: Show an understanding of the concept of food, and the process of digestion and appreciate its importance in humans
Indicator: Identify the end product of digestion of starchy, protein and oily foods and explain how absorption of the digested food occurs in humans
Exemplars:
Observe and describe how digested food is absorbed into the body of humans using animation
Draw a flow chart to show that starch is digested to sugar, protein is digested to amino acids and oils are digested into fatty acids
Perform practical tests on food: starch, glucose, protein and fats and oils

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.2.1: Demonstrate knowledge of the inner planets of the solar system and understand their movement in the system
Indicator: Identify the inner planets of the solar system and describe their properties
Exemplars:
Identify and describe what constitutes the inner planets of the solar system using pictures, videos, etc
Describe the galaxy, milky way, and elliptical shape of the paths of movement of the inner planets
Design and construct a model of the solar system

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.2.1: Demonstrate knowledge of the inner planets of the solar system and understand their movement in the system
Indicator: Discuss the properties and the relative motions of the planets Mercury and Venus
Exemplars:
Outline properties peculiar to each of the planets Mercury and Venus
Describe the movement of the planets Mercury and Venus around the Sun

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.3.1: Recognise the components of and interdependences in an ecosystem, and appreciate their interactions
Indicator: Analyse the components of ecosystems and identify the interactions within
Exemplars:
Describe an ecosystem as a self-sustaining unit in which components interact. E.g. a pond, a forest and many others
Group ecosystems into terrestrial, aquatic and arboreal categories
Identify and list the components, such as biotic and abiotic, of each category of ecosystem
Differentiate among organisms in the different ecosystems mentioned in 2
Explain how the components of the different ecosystems affect one another

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.4.1: Demonstrate an understanding of the differences among the various farming systems: Land Rotation, Crop Rotation, Mixed Cropping, Mixed Farming, and Organic Farming
Indicator: Examine and discuss the differences among the various farming systems
Exemplars:
Identify and define types of farming systems in Ghana and elsewhere
Discuss the characteristics of the different farming systems in Ghana
Compare and contrast the characteristics of the different farming systems

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.4.1: Demonstrate an understanding of the differences among the various farming systems: Land Rotation, Crop Rotation, Mixed Cropping, Mixed Farming, and Organic Farming
Indicator: Categorise different farming systems
Exemplars:
Classify different descriptions of farming systems under Land Rotation, Crop Rotation, Mixed Cropping, Mixed Farming and Organic Farming
Group farming systems prevailing in their community under Land Rotation, Crop Rotation, Mixed Cropping, Mixed Farming and Organic Farming

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.3.4.1: Demonstrate an understanding of the differences among the various farming systems: Land Rotation, Crop Rotation, Mixed Cropping, Mixed Farming, and Organic Farming
Indicator: Discuss the usefulness of different farming systems
Exemplars:
Discuss and tabulate the reasons behind the use of various farming systems
Debate the merits and demerits of the different farming systems

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.1.1: Demonstrate an understanding of forms of energy and their daily applications
Indicator: Identify the various forms of energy and show how they are related
Exemplars:
List forms of energy in terms of Potential, Kinetic, Heat, Sound, Solar, Electrical, Nuclear, Chemical and Light
Demonstrate and show by diagrams how Potential Energy (PE) is related to Kinetic Energy (KE); (Mechanical Energy= PE+ KE)

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.1.1: Demonstrate an understanding of forms of energy and their daily applications
Indicator: Explain daily applications of forms of energy
Exemplars:
Discuss how forms of energy are used in daily life
Match forms of energy to appliances (gadgets) used daily at school, in the home and community
Explain factors that affect Potential and Kinetic energy in their application in daily life
Use mathematical expressions for both Potential energy (PE = mgh) and Kinetic energy (KE = ½ mv2) and use the expressions to solve problems involving mechanical energy

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.1.2: Demonstrate an understanding of the concept of heat transfer and its applications in life
Indicator: Explain and demonstrate how heat is transferred in various media
Exemplars:
Explain how heat is transferred through different media (gas, plastic, metal, liquid)
Carry out an activity to show how heat is transferred through different media

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.1.3: Demonstrate understanding of characteristics of light, such as travelling in a straight line, reflection, refraction and dispersion
Indicator: Demonstrate how light travels in a straight line
Exemplars:
Perform experiments to show that light travels in a straight line and can be reflected and refracted and produce reports, posters or diagrams
Perform an experiment to show dispersion of light into colours

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.2.1: Demonstrate understanding of forms of electricity, its generation and effects on the environment
Indicator: Describe the various forms of electricity generation
Exemplars:
Search for and discuss information about the nature and generation of thermal and nuclear electricity and produce reports, posters, diagrams and charts about your findings

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.2.1: Demonstrate understanding of forms of electricity, its generation and effects on the environment
Indicator: Explain the impact of electricity generation on the environment
Exemplars:
Debate the negative effects of both thermal and nuclear electricity generation on the environment and how to reduce the effects. Create posters leaflets of the outcome of the debate

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.2.2: Demonstrate knowledge of how to assemble and explain the functions of basic electronic components and their interdependence in an electronic circuit
Indicator: Demonstrate how to assemble basic electronic components in an electronic circuit
Exemplars:
Examine electronic components such as types of LEDs, P-N Junction diodes, colour code resistors and capacitors, and arrange them in an electronic circuit

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.2.2: Demonstrate knowledge of how to assemble and explain the functions of basic electronic components and their interdependence in an electronic circuit
Indicator: Discuss the function of each electronic component and their interdependence with each other
Exemplars:
Dismantle and assemble spoilt electronic gadgets such as radio, TV, mobile phones, electronic watches and others that can be found in the home and at school and name the parts
Identify the Positive (P) region and Negative (N) region of the P-N junction diode and construct a simple electronic circuit comprising a 3V battery made of two dry cells in series with a switch and an LED
Explain what happens when the switch in an electronic circuit is closed and when it is opened

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.2.2: Demonstrate knowledge of how to assemble and explain the functions of basic electronic components and their interdependence in an electronic circuit
Indicator: Discuss the function of each electronic component such as resistor, diode, and inductor, and their interdependence for the functioning of an electronic gadget
Exemplars:
Discuss the roles and the significance of the following electronic components in a circuit and how they affect each other: i. LED, ii. Resistor, iii. Diode, and iv. Inductor
Explain changes in brightness in an LED in relation to addition of resistors, diodes, and inductors in an electronic circuit

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.3.1: Demonstrate an understanding of the principle of conservation and conversion of energy and their application in real life situations

Explain the law of conservation of energy by using diagram to show that in a closed system the value of chemical energy, for example in dry cell which changes into electrical, heat and light energy will remain the same. 2. Use 1 to explain energy conversion and its application to life

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.3.1: Demonstrate an understanding of the principle of conservation and conversion of energy and their application in real life situations

Illustrate everyday use of conversion of energy and show diagrammatically the conversion of energy to other forms

subject: Science
content:

Describe how energy is conserved and explain how it can be done for the benefit of humans and other life forms

subject: Science

Demonstrate how unbalanced forces cause motion

Research to find what Newton's first law is and discuss it

subject: Science

Indicator: Examine the application of Newton's First Law of motion in life
Exemplars:
Discuss some applications of Newton's First Law of Motion. E.g. when a metallic ball is put on a smooth surface and given a push it will be in motion until it gets to a blockade and it stops. Use of seat belts in a vehicle, etc
Explain the importance of Newton's First Law of Motion

subject: Science
content:

Demonstrate the characteristics (Repulsive, attractive, and orientation N-S direction) of a magnet
Discuss the uses of magnet in everyday life

subject: Science

List examples of simple machines

subject: Science

Indicator: Describe the types and functions of levers
Exemplars:
Name the types of levers and explain their general functions
Classify levers into first, second and third classes and demonstrate how the principals involved in each class make work easier in everyday life

subject: Science
content:

Indicator: Know work input, and output and efficiency as they apply to machines
Exemplars:
Explain the terms work input, work output and efficiency
Explain efficiency of a machine as the ratio of work output to work input expressed as a percentage

Describe how efficiency of simple machines can be improved (e.g. by oiling its parts to reduce friction)

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.5.1: Demonstrate knowledge and skills in handling and maintenance of basic and simple agricultural tools

List some simple or basic farm tools in agriculture (give examples found in animal and crop farms)
Discuss the meaning and importance of handling and maintenance of agricultural tools
List and match the basic rules in handling and maintenance of tools with specific simple tools used in agriculture
Describe how handling and maintenance of simple and basic agricultural tools are done

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.4.5.1: Demonstrate knowledge and skills in handling and maintenance of basic and simple agricultural tools
Indicator: Apply the handling and maintenance of basic and simple agricultural tools in their community
Exemplars:
Observe and discuss the handling and maintenance of basic and simple agricultural tools used in farms visited in the community and write a report
Assemble agricultural tools from the community and practice handling the tools to perform simple agricultural operations. Writedown the operational rules of handling agricultural tools
Assemble agricultural tools from the community and practice the basic rules in tools maintenance and list the rules used

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.5.1.1: Exhibit knowledge and skill of scientific basis for management practices of types of waste in the environment

Research for information on good waste management practices and use it to carry out a project to make the environment clean
Write a report for presentation on the outcome of the project carried out in 1
Discuss how to manage types of waste and explain the science underlying it

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.5.2.1: Demonstrate knowledge of common deficiency diseases of humans, their causes, symptoms, effects and prevention
Indicator: Explain the relationship between food nutrients and common deficiency diseases and how they affect humans
Exemplars:
Name and analyse food nutrients such as carbohydrates, proteins, fatty acids, and their uses in the human body
Discuss and make presentations on deficiency diseases associated with lack of food nutrients such as carbohydrates, proteins, fatty acids, vitamins and others in the human body
Relate the nutrients they gain or lack to the foods they normally eat e.g. lack of protein leads to kwashiorkor, lack of iron lead to anaemia, etc
Describe symptoms, effects and prevention of common deficiency diseases such as night blindness, rickets, scurvy, kwashiorkor and others

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.5.2.2: Demonstrate knowledge of the nature of selected viral, diseases of humans, their causes, symptoms, effects and management
Indicator: Explain the nature of viral diseases with special emphasis on corona virus (COVID-19) /Ebola/H1N1 disease its causes, symptoms, effects on humans and its prevention
Exemplars:
Discuss the nature of viral diseases
Search for information and make presentations on the corona virus disease (COVID -19), Ebola, and H1N1 diseases their mode of transmission from person to person, community to community and from country to country
Describe the symptoms, effects and prevention of COVID-19), Ebola, and H1N1 diseases and why they are declared pandemic
Describe the role of individuals, community members and government in managing COVID-19 Ebola, and H1N1 diseases
Design and produce a poster to educate their community members on the incidence and control of named viral diseases: COVID-19, Ebola, and H1N1. B.7. 5.3.1.1 Discover and explain how careers in science can improve human conditions and relate these careers to the work of great national and international scientists and science educators
Describe various careers in science and relate them to the work of national scientists. E.g. Prof. Ibok Oduro, Prof. Francis Allotey, Prof. Ewurama Addy, and Science Educationists: Prof. Anamuah-Mensah, Prof. Theophilus Ossei-Anto, Prof. Christian Anthony-Krueger and others
Describe various careers in science and relate them to the work of international scientists: Albert Einstein, Alexander Fleming, Charles Darwin, Paul Ratnei, Stephen Hawkins, etc. through presentations
Research, and build portfolio on the impact of science and technology and innovation in homes, schools, communities, and the universe and make a presentation
Identify the science and technology careers that Ghana must focus on and give reasons

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.5.4.1: Demonstrate understanding of sustainable energy choices and their impact on the environment
Indicator: Search for information on ways sustainable energy choices and scientific ideas are used to protect the environment
Exemplars:
Describe how people use sustainable energy choices and scientific ideas to protect the environment
Analyse greenhouse effects on the environment and show how they can be minimised
Design a project to show how energy can be locally sustained through the use of scientific processes to protect the environment

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.5.5.1: Demonstrate understanding of different plants and animals found in different land forms and how they survive (with emphasis land forms in Ghana)

Exemplars:
Identify different types of plants and animals found in different landforms (plateau plain, mountain valley and others)
Describe the characteristics that enable different types of animals to live in different landforms (plateau plain, mountain valley and others)
Describe the characteristics that enable different types of plants to survive in different landforms (plateau plain, mountain valley and others)
Make an album of different types of plants and animals that live in different landforms (plateau plain, mountain valley and others)

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B7.5.5.1: Demonstrate understanding of different plants and animals found in different land forms and how they survive (with emphasis land forms in Ghana)
Indicator: Explain the nature of associations that exist among plants and animals in different landforms and their mechanisms for survival
Exemplars:
Describe the nature of associations such as mutualism, parasitism, commensalism among plants and animals and explain the effects on their habitats
Carry out research about the different ways that different plants and animals survive in the landforms in which they are found. BASIC 8

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.1.1.1: Demonstrate knowledge of types of mixtures, and understanding of the processes of scientific ways of separating the components of mixtures
Indicator: Identify types of mixtures by name and characteristics
Exemplars:
Group materials such as powder, pebbles, bottle tops, salt, sugar, sand, gari, gravel, oil, water and others into two main categories: solids and liquids
Put any two of the materials (in 1) together and describe the resultant nature of the product formed
Draw observable conclusions on homogeneous and heterogeneous characteristics from mixtures of two or more materials such as sand and gravel; sand and water; oil and water
Compare and contrast solutes and solvents based on their physical characteristics

Identify a suspension as a type of mixture e.g. mixture of groundnut paste and water in a glass
Differentiate between a colloid and a suspension and show the colloidal effect

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.1.1.1: Demonstrate knowledge of types of mixtures, and understanding of the processes of scientific ways of separating the components of mixtures
Indicator: Design and perform processes for separating kinds of mixtures
Exemplars:
Perform activities such as distilling, filtering, sieving and others to separate different kinds of mixtures and present a report on your findings using drawing and written work

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.1.1.2: Demonstrate understanding of atoms and the atomic structure of elements in the periodic table
Indicator: Describe atoms as composed of sub-atomic particles
Exemplars:
Explain an atom and its structure of an element using/linking it to the periodic table
List the sub-atomic particles found in the atom and indicate their location in the atom (e.g. proton, electron, neutron)
State the electrical charges on the sub-atomic particles
Describe the differences between the atomic number and the mass number of elements
Determine the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in an atom

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.1.1.2: Demonstrate understanding of atoms and the atomic structure of elements in the periodic table
Indicator: Explain the arrangement of elements in terms of the number of protons in the nuclei of atoms of each element
Exemplars:
Explain how elements are arranged in order of the number of protons using the periodic table
Draw the distribution of electrons (electron configuration) in the atoms
Explain the formation of ions
Describe a molecule as a combination of atoms

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.1.2.1: Demonstrate an understanding of the types of cells and their structure in relation to different organisms
Indicator: Examine and describe the structure of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
Exemplars:
Compare and contrast prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
Create a table to show a chart or a slideshow depicting images and labels of the types of cells. Identify their differences and similarities after observation
Draw and label a prokaryotic cell and a eukaryotic cell and make a presentation on what is observed

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.1.2.1: Demonstrate an understanding of the types of cells and their structure in relation to different organisms
Indicator: Classify organisms (plants or animals) as prokaryotic or eukaryotic based on the type of cells they are made of
Exemplars:
Observe and list examples of organisms; plants and animals as prokaryotic or eukaryotic based on each cell type
Explain the impact of prokaryotes and eukaryotes on humans health and devise safety measures to protect them

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.2.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of the process of Carbon cycle as an example of repeated pattern of change in nature and how it relates to the environment
Indicator: Explain the process of the carbon cycle
Exemplars:
Identify the carbon cycle from the internet, charts or pictures and write short notes on what happens at each stage
Produce a flow chart to trace the process of the carbon cycle in nature
Explain the process of the carbon cycle depicting processes such as a) Photosynthesis b) Respiration c) Burning d) Decay
Compile information on the carbon cycle and give reasons why it is a repeated pattern e.g. it is because the carbon is circulated continuously in the environment

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.2.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of the process of Carbon cycle as an example of repeated pattern of change in nature and how it relates to the environment
Indicator: Describe the role of the carbon cycle to the environment
Exemplars:
Describe the role of the carbon cycle in maintaining balance in the composition of air in the environment. E.g. plants absorb carbon in the form of Carbon (IV) Oxide from the air for photosynthesis and oxygen is produced for respiration and in return, respiration gives out carbon in the form of Carbon (IV) Oxide. Note: Discuss photosynthesis and respiration in plants as part of the carbon cycle
Explain the effect of the carbon cycle on food chains, using diagrams
Describe the relationship between greenhouse gases and the carbon cycle

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.2.2.1: Demonstrate an activity to show the life cycle of the Anopheles mosquito and show how the effects of the mosquito on humans can be managed
Indicator: Describe the life cycle and economic importance of the Anopheles mosquito
Exemplars:
Observe and draw the different stages of the life cycle of the Anopheles mosquito e.g. by breeding the mosquito in a glass jar
Describe the economic importance of the Anopheles mosquito

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B8.2.2.1: Demonstrate an activity to show the life cycle of the Anopheles mosquito and show how the effects of the mosquito on humans can be managed
Indicator: Discuss the impact of the Anopheles mosquito on humans and how it can be controlled
Exemplars:
Discuss the impact of the female Anopheles mosquito as a vector of plasmodium on humans
Generate solutions to control malaria in Ghana

subject: Science
content:

Observe and discuss different seed beds for planting different crops

Match the types of seed beds with the types and stages of crops planted in your community

Observe and discuss the practice of planting different crops in different seed beds
Select different plant parts, (seeds, seedlings, cuttings, leaves, roots) and plant them in different seed beds

subject: Science
content:

Write and give presentations on the reasons for differences in the heights, sizes, number of flowers and fruits of plants grown in different seed beds

subject: Science
content:

Predict what will happen to animals who are not provided with adequate water

Demonstrate proper ways of cleaning the teeth

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.2.2: Demonstrate understanding of the relationship of health and disease, the concept of common diseases in the environment and how to control them
Indicator: Explain the concepts of health and disease and show their relationship
Exemplars:
Define health as stipulated by World Health Organisation (WHO) and show the relationship between health and disease

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.2.2: Demonstrate understanding of the relationship of health and disease, the concept of common diseases in the environment and how to control them
Indicator: Explain the concept of common diseases in an environment
Exemplars:
Conduct a survey about common diseases and analyse the findings to show what constitutes a common disease in a community
Identify causes, symptoms and prevention of common diseases

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.2.2: Demonstrate knowledge of selected fungal, diseases of humans, their causes, symptoms, effects and prevention
Indicator: Explain the nature of fungal diseases with special emphasis on Ringworm/candidiasis/fingernail, and toe nail infection, their causes, symptoms, effects on humans and its prevention
Exemplars:
Discuss the nature of fungal diseases
Search for information and make presentations on ringworm, candidiasis and fungal eye infection diseases their mode of transmission from person to person, community to community and from country to country
Describe the symptoms, effects and prevention of ringworm, candidiasis and fungal eye infection diseases
Describe the role of individuals, community members and government in managing ringworm, candidiasis and fungal eye infection diseases
Design and produce a poster to educate their community members on the incidence and control of named fungal diseases: ringworm, candidiasis and fungal eye infection

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.3.1: Analyse the scientific concepts, principles and processes applied in industries in and outside their community
Indicator: Investigate the scientific concepts, principles and processes involved in industries in their environment
Exemplars:
Identify products of industries within and outside their community and describe the process of production
Investigate and outline scientific concepts, principles and processes underlying the production of common everyday industrial products

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.3.2: Demonstrate an understanding of the concept of industry, the science underpinning the processes of production in industries the technologies in indigenous industries and western industries
Indicator: Explain the concept of industry and distinguish between modern and indigenous industries
Exemplars:
Identify an industry as individual firms producing the same commodity and give examples of industries in their community
Describe how technology affects industry and compare the technologies in indigenous and modern industries

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.3.2: Demonstrate an understanding of the concept of industry, the science underpinning the processes of production in industries the technologies in indigenous industries and western industries
Indicator: Examine indigenous industries in their communities and show the scientific processes in the stages of production
Exemplars:
Discuss indigenous industries in their communities and identify the scientific processes, concepts and principles underlying the stages of production in the industries
Identify indigenous practices at home, school and the community and the science involved in the practices

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.4.1: Demonstrate an understanding of the natural and human factors that influence climate change and a green economy
Indicator: Examine various natural and human factors that influence climate change and green economy in their localities
Exemplars:
Identify the natural factors that influence climate change
Describe ways of minimising human activities that influence climate change
Compare natural and human factors that influence climate change and green economy

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.4.2: Evaluate the effectiveness of initiatives that address the issue of climate change and green economy in Ghana and the world at large
Indicator: Assess data on climate change and green economy actions/ activities globally including Ghana and other countries
Exemplars:
Research into climate change and green economy actions in Ghana
Access climate change and green economy actions in other countries
Compare and contrast climate change and green economy actions in Ghana and other countries
Identify and write the effective initiatives that address climate change and green economy issues in Ghana and other countries
Prescribe with reasons best practices to serve as possible solutions to address climate change and green economy issues in Ghana

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.5.1: Demonstrate knowledge and skills in the use of plant roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes APPENDICES
Indicator: Show and list the uses of different plant parts for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes
Exemplars:
Identify plant parts that are used for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes
Describe how plant parts are used for agricultural and non- agricultural purposes
List the uses of plant parts for agricultural purposes (such as planting, tools, animal housing, animal feed, soil improvement, pest and disease control, etc.)
List the uses of plant parts for non-agricultural purposes (such as herbal medicine, construction of houses, bridges and furniture, artefacts, ceremonies, rituals, education, etc.)

subject: Science
content:
Content standard B9.5.5.1: Demonstrate knowledge and skills in the use of plant roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes APPENDICES
Indicator: Demonstrate the use of different plant parts for agricultural and non-agricultural purposes
Exemplars:
Create agricultural materials from different plant parts that are used to carry out agricultural activities
Create non-agricultural materials from different plant parts to carry out non-agricultural activities

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.1.1.1: Demonstrate skills in dealing with environmental challenges
Indicator: Examine ways of dealing with sanitation challenges in the environment
Exemplars:
Explain: i. Environment ii. Sanitation
Discuss the types of environment (physical and social)
Identify some environmental problems, including poor sanitation
Examine cultural practices and their related problems for sanitation in the community
Discuss the effects of poor sanitation practices
Identify different ways of managing sanitation problems
Embark on a project with the aim of managing sanitation problems in the community

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.1.1.2: Examine the sources of energy and demonstrate the skills of conserving energy in Ghana
Indicator: Examine the sources of energy
Exemplars:
Explain energy
Through the use of internet, videos or pictures, describe the sources of energy in Ghana, including fuel wood, hydro, solar and thermal
In groups, categorise sources of energy into renewable and non-renewable
Examine the benefits of using renewable energy
Examine the benefits of using non-renewable energy sources
In groups, let learners discuss and design posters to show how different sources of energy are used
In groups, let learners discuss how sun or wind can be used to heat or perform work
Through group discussion, come out with ways of using energy
In groups, discuss why Ghana sometimes imports energy

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.1.2.1: Demonstrate a range of mapping skills
Indicator: Demonstrate skills involved in mapping and locating places in the environment
Exemplars:
Explain the following concepts: "maps" and "scale"
Identify types of maps, including street maps, maps showing landscape features and national maps using an atlas
Explore the importance of maps to different people, including airline managers, fisherfolk, farmers and, for example, a family which has moved from a rural area to a city
Identify components of maps, including north arrow, scale, map key allowing representation of physical features (including rivers, lakes, mountains and coastline) and human features (including settlements, plantations and industrial developments) using names, symbols and colours
Sketch a map of the school compound, marking the main features
Locate some important landmarks in the community using maps. For example, the bank is 500 metres north of the Junior High School

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.1.3.1: Show understanding of the world around us
Indicator: Examine major physical features of the earth
Exemplars:
Identify some major features of the earth such as mountain ranges, rivers, oceans, hot deserts and tropical rainforest
With the use of maps, find the locations of the following major physical features: i. Mountain ranges, including Akuapim-Togo, Gambaga, Kwahu, Himalayas, Rockies, Andes and Alps ii. Rivers, including the River Bia, Tano, Ankobra, Pra, Densu, Volta, Nile, Niger, Congo, Ganges, Yangtze, Amazon, Mississippi iii. Oceans: Atlantic, Arctic, Southern, Indian, Pacific iv. Hot deserts, including Sahara, Kalahari, Gobi, Arabian v. Tropical rainforests, including the Amazon Rainforest
Discuss human activities that affect the following features and ways of protecting them: i. Major mountain ranges ii. Rivers iii. Oceans
Discuss the effects of plastic pollution on water bodies including streams, ponds, rivers, dams, lakes and oceans

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.1.3.2: Assess the issue of natural disasters and their management
Indicator: Examine natural disasters in the environment
Exemplars:
Explain natural disasters
Watch documentaries on some natural disasters
Mention examples of natural disasters, including flood, drought, landslide, wildfire, earthquake and sea erosion
Identify natural disasters in Ghana
Suggest ways to manage disasters
Discuss the role of institutions responsible for early detection and management of natural disasters in Ghana, including Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMA), National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO)

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.2.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of adolescent behaviour and reproductive health issues
Indicator: Examine issues on adolescent behaviour and reproductive health
Exemplars:
Explain the concepts: i. Adolescence ii. Reproductive Health
Discuss adolescent behaviours, including chastity that would support reproductive health
Discuss in groups why healthy behaviour during adolescence is important, both for the individual and for the country as a whole
Invite a resource person, such as a doctor or nurse, to talk about how some adolescent behaviours can harm their reproductive health and cause other problems
Explain changes that adolescents go through (physical, cognitive, social and emotional)
Discuss some challenges faced by adolescents

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.2.3.1: Exhibit knowledge of the importance of socialisation
Indicator: Examine the place of socialisation in developing the individual
Exemplars:
Explain the meaning of socialisation (adapting behaviour to the norms of a culture or society)
Explain the terms: i. Agencies ii. Agents
Identify the agencies and agents of socialisation, including family, schools, parents and teachers
Discuss the roles of agencies and agents in the socialisation process
Role-play and embark on a socialising project involving the school and the community
With the use of the Internet, let learners find out the need for socialisation and the challenges associated with it

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.2.4.1: Analyse the population structure in Ghana and its related issues
Indicator: Examine the components of population growth
Exemplars:
Explain the concept of population growth
Discuss how population in Ghana has changed in the recent past
Compare Ghana's population growth with that of some other countries in Africa and in the world
Discuss the following factors of population change: i. Birth rate ii. Death rate iii. Migration
Investigate the causes of the following in Ghana: i. High birth rates ii. High death rates

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.3.1.1: Show understanding of self as a unique individual
Indicator: Exhibit knowledge of self-identity
Exemplars:
Explain the concepts "self " and "self-identity"
Identify attitudes that enhance self-worth, including self-confidence, can-do spirit and a positive attitude towards life
Identify one's strengths and weaknesses as unique individual and discuss with one's peers
Examine the reasons for knowing oneself including accepting oneself and identification of one's potential and abilities
Describe how an individual can develop their capabilities, including education and training, counselling, continuous practice, etc

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.4.1.1: Analyse the responsibilities of a citizen
Indicator: Examine the value of citizenship in nation building
Exemplars:
Explain the concept of "citizenship"
Discuss the various ways of acquiring citizenship in Ghana, including citizenship by birth, adoption, registration and naturalisation
Examine the responsibilities of a Ghanaian citizen, including obeying rules and regulations, protecting state property, reporting crime, respecting national symbols and payment of taxes, among others
In groups, discuss good working attitudes, including honesty, willingness to report crime and being punctual and regular at events and at the workplace
Dramatise the various ways (communal labour, reporting crime) citizens contribute to the development of the country

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.5.1.1: Demonstrate knowledge of human resource development in Ghana
Indicator: Mention ways of developing human resource in Ghana
Exemplars:
Explain the concepts: i. Human resource ii. Human resource development
Identify ways of developing human resource in Ghana, including education, training and retraining, career counselling, performing leadership roles and mentoring
Discuss the importance of human resource development in Ghana
Assess the challenges associated with human resource development in Ghana
Suggest solutions to problems facing human resource development in Ghana

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.5.2.1: Demonstrate understanding of social security and pension issues
Indicator: Examine the importance of social security to the individual
Exemplars:
Explain the concept of social security
Discuss the features of social security, including the law which established it
Identify types of social security schemes, including the Pension Fund
Think-pair-share the benefits of social security to the individual
Create a poster on the benefits of social security

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.5.3.1: Demonstrate knowledge on how tourism and leisure promote national development
Indicator: Examine the role of tourism and leisure in socio- economic development of Ghana
Exemplars:
Explain the concepts: i. Tourism ii. Leisure
Identify some attractive places or sceneries in your locality
Examine reasons for which people go on tour to different places
Discuss the economic and social importance of tourism to the nation's development
Explain challenges faced in the tourism industry
Suggest ways of solving the challenges faced in the tourism industry
Discuss ways of promoting tourism in Ghana

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.6.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of how Ghana became an independent nation
Indicator: Explain how events after the 1948 riots accelerated the move towards independence
Exemplars:
Show documentaries or listen to personal accounts on the 28th February riots in Accra. OR Visit the spot where the ex-servicemen were killed
Discuss the documentaries or what was witnessed on the visit
Discuss the reasons for the formation of the Watson commission
Examine how the Watson Commission helped the move towards independence
With the use of the Internet or any other sources of information, write down the bio data of the three ex-service men (Sgt. Adjetey, Sgt. Odartey Lamptey and Corporal Attipoe) and how this can inspire learners

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.6.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of how Ghana became an independent nation
Indicator: Recount the formation of the Convention People's Party (CPP) in 1949
Exemplars:
With the use of internet/pictures show and discuss pictures of Kwame Nkrumah, Kojo Botsio and K.A. Gbedemah as leaders of the CPP
Discuss the role of other groups, including trade unions, 'veranda boys' in the activities of the CPP
Use resource persons, including retired educationalists, veteran soldiers, retired police officers and senior citizens to tell them about the 'Positive Action' OR find out from the community/parents what is meant by 'Positive Action'
In groups, create a poster on one of the following personalities indicating their bio data including the position they occupied in government: Kwame Nkrumah, K. A. Gbedemah and Kojo Botsio

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.6.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of how Ghana became an independent nation
Indicator: Discuss the recommendations of the Coussey Committee and the outcomes of the 1951, 1954 and 1956 elections
Exemplars:
Discuss how the Coussey Committee recommendations formed the basis of the 1950 Constitution
Using sources of evidence including YouTube- https://www.eaumf.org/ ejm-blog/2018/2/15/february-13-1951-gov-sir-charles-arden-clarke- invites-nkrumah-to-form-a-government, discuss the outcome of the 1951 elections and why Kwame Nkrumah was released from prison
Discuss the role of Kwame Nkrumah as leader of government business (1951 up to 1952)
Examine why a new constitution was drawn up in 1954 (for example, the CPP was dissatisfied with the provisions of the 1950 constitution and called for a new constitution to be drawn up for the Gold Coast)
Discuss what happened after the CPP won the 1956 election

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B7.6.1.1: Demonstrate understanding of how Ghana became an independent nation
Indicator: Analyse the nature of government from 1957 to 1960
Exemplars:
Discuss the power-sharing arrangement between the British government and elected Ghanaian officials
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of power-sharing from March 1957 to July 1960
Use the Internet and other sources of information to find out the portfolios held by British officials and Ghanaian officials from 1957 to 1960
Discuss the composition of the cabinet from March 1957 to July 1960. DL 6.3: Use digital tools to create novel things. CP 5.1: Ability to combine information and ideas from several sources to reach a conclusion. CP 8.4: Ability to identify important and appropriate criteria and use them to evaluate available alternatives. CC 8.3: Apply appropriate diction and structure sentences correctly for narrative, persuasive, imaginative and expository purposes

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.1.1.1: Demonstrate skills in dealing with environmental challenges
Indicator: Examine water pollution as an environmental challenge
Exemplars:
Explain pollution
Watch a documentary of polluted water bodies for discussion
Discuss the causes of water pollution, including human, animal and industrial waste
Examine the effects of water pollution, including death of fish and the contamination of water leading to diseases such as cholera, typhoid and dysentery
Presentation on the need and how to prevent water pollution

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.1.1.2: Analyse the sources and ways of conserving energy in Ghana
Indicator: Examine the means of conserving energy
Exemplars:
Explain energy conservation
Discuss responsible use of energy to minimise economic and environmental costs
Role play how different members of the community might conserve energy (e.g. a parent of four, a headteacher, a shopkeeper)
Debate the need for energy conservation
Apply the knowledge and skills acquired to help conserve energy in learners' homes and school, including turning off the light when not in use, ironing things in bulk, among others
Project work: Use sun or wind to generate energy

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.1.3.1: Demonstrate understanding of the significance of weather and climate to the environment
Indicator: Assess the significance of weather and climate to the environment
Exemplars:
Explain the concepts: i. Climate ii. Weather
Discuss the elements of climate, including temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure and precipitation
Discuss various ways of measuring the elements of weather from several sources to reach a conclusion. and climate, including the use of hygrometer, rain gauge and CP 5.2: Analyse and make distinct judgment about barometer
Sketch the map of Ghana and indicate the different climatic zones
Discuss the world climatic zones
Examine the factors that affect climate, including latitude, altitude and distance from the sea

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.1.3.2: Demonstrate understanding of natural disasters and their management
Indicator: Discuss natural disasters
Exemplars:
Watch some documentaries on natural disasters
Examine natural disasters and share the understanding of the term, including the idea that it involves great damage and also loss of lives. Examples of natural disasters are flooding, rainstorms, earthquake, volcanoes, wildfires and drought
Examine the causes of flooding, including human action. For example urban development which can make flooding more likely or more extreme
Investigate the effects of flooding on the environment
Carry out a project to raise awareness in the community about the need for certain flood control measures and careful planning of any new development

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.1.2.1: Demonstrate skills in sketching maps and interpreting landscapes from maps
Indicator: Sketch maps and interpret landscapes from maps
Exemplars:
Sketch a map of your school compound
Draw a diagram showing an eight-point compass (showing North, South, East and West; North East, North West, South East, South West)
Using a map with grid squares, locate some important landmarks
Draw/ sketch the map of the community indicating important landmarks
Sketch a map of the school compound to scale
Show directions to important places in the community
Sketch maps showing the positions or directions to your home using a compass directions

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.2.2.1: Show understanding of the family and family life issues
Indicator: Examine the composition and functions of the nuclear and the extended families
Exemplars:
Explain the concept of family
Differentiate nuclear from extended family systems
Identify the roles of various members of the nuclear family
Explain the roles of the extended family
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the nuclear family systems
Compare the Ghanaian family system and that of any country in the Western world
In groups, discuss the importance of the family as an institution
Discuss the role of the family in supporting gender equality

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.2.2.1: Show understanding of the family and family life issues
Indicator: Discuss the issues of inheritance in Ghana
Exemplars:
In pairs, discuss the concept of inheritance and share thoughts with the class
Identify and discuss the systems of inheritance in Ghana, including matrilineal, patrilineal and Intestate Succession
Invite a resource person in the community to talk about any of the systems of inheritance
Discuss the positive and negative effects of the inheritance systems in Ghana
Suggest ways of improving the indigenous inheritance system
Role play one system of inheritance in Ghana
Debate the Intestate Succession law versus the indigenous inheritance system in Ghana

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.2.4.1: Analyse the population structure in Ghana and its related issues
Indicator: Compare the population structure of high-income and middle/low income countries
Exemplars:
Explain what population structure means
Draw/sketch the population structure of your school
Examine the population structure of Ghana as set out in a population pyramid
Examine the population structure of any developed country in the world, for example, China, Norway, Sweden, Singapore, Japan, and Canada
Discuss the population structures of low, middle and high-income countries
Suggest reasons for the population pyramids of low, middle and high- income countries with different shapes, including smaller families, higher standards of living, and high-quality healthcare

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.3.2.1: Demonstrate knowledge of the role of the individual in the community
Indicator: Examine the role of the individuals in the community
Exemplars:
Explain the concept of community
Watch a documentary about different communities and discuss observations
Explain what community development involves (the values vision, initiative and drive in the process of community development)
Explain the factors to be considered in community decision-making process, including investigating, developing and evaluating alternatives
Invite a resource person to talk about the importance of community development
Identify a specific need or problem of the community and show how learners can help solve it

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.3.2.1: Demonstrate knowledge of the role of the individual in the community
Indicator: Discuss the relevance of volunteerism to community development
Exemplars:
Explain the concept of volunteerism
Examine the ways by which one can volunteer in the community responsibly, including performing household chores, shopping or cleaning for an elderly person and helping clean the community
Identify some volunteering roles in the community and their contribution to community development, including reporting crime in the community to the police and avoiding taking the law into one's own hands
Discuss the importance of volunteerism to socio-economic development of the community
Project work: form voluntary clubs and discuss their functions within the community
Do a voluntary work in the community and write a report on it

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.4.1.1: Investigate the rights and responsibilities of a citizen
Indicator: Examine the importance of human rights in the Ghanaian society
Exemplars:
Explain the concept "human rights"
Examine the United Nations declaration on human rights
Identify some examples of human rights enshrined in the 1992 constitution
Assess the importance of the protection of human rights
Examine the rights and responsibilities of a citizen. Rights Right to life Right to education Right to work
Role play rights and responsibilities of citizens
Undertake a project in the community on citizens' rights and how to safeguard them (collect data on human right issues in the community). DL 5.1: Ability to ascertain when information is

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.4.2.1: Analyse ways of preventing and managing conflict
Indicator: Examine ways of preventing and managing conflict in the community
Exemplars:
Explain the following terms: i. Conflict ii. Conflict prevention iii. Conflict management
Watch and discuss video or pictures on conflict and its effects on the larger society
Identify and discuss some causes of conflict in your community
Discuss the effects of conflict in your community
Examine attitudes and values needed to prevent conflict in your community
Assess the role of women in conflict prevention and management
Suggest ways to manage conflict situations in your community

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.5.2.1: Demonstrate understanding of employer and employee relations in social security and pension
Indicator: Exhibit knowledge on employer and employee relation in social security and pension schemes
Exemplars:
Explain the following concepts: i. Employment ii. Employer iii. Employee
Discuss the obligations of an employer in social security and pension schemes, including registering employees and paying their contributions regularly
In groups, discuss the obligations of an employee towards social security and pension schemes, including checking statement of contribution regularly and updating their records

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.5.3.1: Evaluate tourism as an important economic sector for national development
Indicator: Assess the importance of tourism to socio-economic development of Ghana
Exemplars:
Use videos/pictures to identify some tourist sites
Visit tourist sites and suggest ways of improving them
Discuss how new tourist sites can be developed
Examine the importance of tourism to socio-economic development
Compare the development of tourism between: i. Ghana and Kenya ii. Ghana and United Kingdom

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.6.2.1: Analyse the main developments in the Republics between 1960 and 1972
Indicator: Explain how the First Republic came into being
Exemplars:
Use the Internet, print media and oral sources to find out how the First Republic was established
Discuss the outcome of 27 April 1960 referendum
Discuss the outcome of 27 April 1960 presidential elections
Dramatise the inauguration of Kwame Nkrumah as president of the First Republic on 1 July 1960
Produce a chart showing major political events from 1951 to1960

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.6.2.1: Analyse the main developments in the Republics between 1960 and 1972
Indicator: Explain political developments under the first republic
Exemplars:
Identify the main features of the 1960 Constitution of the First Republic
Examine the changes that happened in the country as a result of the 1960 Constitution of the First Republic. For example the introduction of a presidential system of government
Debate the effects of the changes in the 1960 Republican Constitution on the status of the country. For example, the introduction of a presidential system of government
Describe the membership of the cabinet under the1960 Constitution

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.6.2.1: Analyse the main developments in the Republics between 1960 and 1972
Indicator: Explain how the Second Republic came into being
Exemplars:
Use the internet, print media and oral sources to find out how the Second Republic was established
Discuss the outcome of the 1969 general elections
Dramatise the handing over of power from the National Liberation Council (NLC) to Dr K. A Busia's Progress Party
Compare the First Republican Constitution and the second Republican Constitution

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B8.6.2.1: Analyse the main developments in the Republics between 1960 and 1972
Indicator: Explain political developments under the Second Republic
Exemplars:
Describe the main features of the 1969 Constitution of the Second Republic including the creation of the office of the Prime Minister
Explain the changes that happened in the country as a result of the 1969 Constitution of the Second Republic
Discuss the membership of the cabinet under the1969 Constitution

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B9.1.1.1: Demonstrate skills in dealing with environmental challenges
Indicator: Examine air pollution as an environmental challenge
Exemplars:
Explain what air pollution means
Identify activities in the environment that lead to air pollution, including fumes from vehicles, industry and smoke from fires
Discuss the effects of air pollution, including causing health problems such as asthma
Discuss ways to prevent air pollution
Do a project in the community to educate members on the ways to reduce air pollution

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B9.1.1.2: Evaluate the sources and ways of conserving energy
Indicator: Assess global sources and the means of conserving energy
Exemplars:
Identify global energy sources and conservation in countries such as Ghana, United Kingdom, Germany
With the use of the Internet, research alternative energy sources and do a presentation in class
Discuss gender issues related to energy production, supply and usage (Access to energy resources affects quality of life; some segments of the society are more vulnerable to impact of energy choices than others)
Describe the processes and devices for measuring and metering energy consumption
In groups, create posters on the advantages of energy conservation to educate others in the community, including saving money, making the most of our scarce energy resources and reducing air pollution
Present a report on energy conservation education that you have undertaken

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B9.1.4.1: Investigate the natural and human resources around us
Indicator: Examine the importance of natural resources to the development of Ghana
Exemplars:
Explain what is meant by natural resources
Through the use of videos or pictures, identify the natural resources of the country, including renewable (for example timber) and non- renewable resources (such as gold, bauxite and oil)
On the map of Ghana, show the location of the natural resources
Discuss efficient ways of exploiting natural resources
Explain the importance of natural resources for the development of the country
Discuss the difficulty in exploiting natural resources effectively, including low level of technology, limited technical expertise and limited capital resources

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B9.1.4.1: Investigate the natural and human resources around us
Indicator: Evaluate the importance of human resources to the development of Ghana
Exemplars:
Explain what is meant by human resource
Identify ways of developing human resource
Through group work, discuss why an educated and trained human resource is the most important asset of the country
Explain how Ghana's human resource can be efficiently used in the production of goods and services
Investigate how some people in the community use their human resource abilities to help the community develop
Suggest new ways by which they would use their human resource abilities to help develop the community

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B9.2.2.1: Evaluate the institution of marriage in Ghana
Indicator: Examine the importance of marriage as a social institution in Ghana
Exemplars:
Explain the concept of marriage as a social institution (other social institutions include the family and religious sects)
Discuss ways of contracting marriages in Ghana
Identify the ways in which marriage is important as a social institution, including providing a stable, loving setting for children to be brought up and helping to provide economic support for parents
Investigate the causes of broken marriages
Dramatise the effects of broken marriages on the family structure (such as teenage pregnancy, drug abuse and truancy)
Suggest ways of sustaining marriages

subject: Social Studies
content:
Content standard B9.2.2.2: Assess the need for responsible parenting in the family
Indicator: Examine the importance of responsible parenting within the family system
Exemplars:
Explain the concepts: i. Parenthood ii. Parenting
Differentiate parenthood from parenting
Discuss the responsibilities of parents including providing food, clothes, shelter and a loving and stable environment for the upbringing of children
Discuss inappropriate parenting behaviour and its consequences, including failure to provide the basic needs of children,. For example, drunkenness
Examine how some behaviours by children can cause their parents to act inappropriately for example, disobedience, indiscipline, refusal to go to school and perform house chores
Suggest ways for handling parent-child conflicts, including dialogue, effective communication
Carry out an education programme in the community on the need for parents to be responsible

subject: Social Studies
content:

content:

Explain the concept of national identity
Sing patriotic songs and discuss how songs promote national identity

Discuss ways of fostering national unity and defending the integrity of the nation
